In a black hole, time might end, or loop, or become a place in space, or become wildly unpredictable. And us physicists cannot agree which one actually happens.

I think most people when they’re taught about black holes are taught a simplified version, that you fall in, and you end up in the middle crushed into an infinitely small point, a singularity. Which as you’re falling towards does weird things to time.

But that describes a version of black holes that don’t exist in the real Universe (the Schwarzschild solution).

Real black holes spin, and spin changes everything. Including the nature of the singularity itself, which becomes a donut shape (the Kerr solution).

At least, an infinitely thin donut. Which does even weirder things to time, perhaps even making time travel possible.

I’m going to walk you through first what is a black hole, what happens to time in a non-rotating black hole? What actually happens to time in a more realistic rotating black hole? And why physicists cannot agree on what’s going on, and hope that if we only had a theory of quantum gravity we might be able to solve this...

Papers mentioned:
Hamilton & Avelino (2010) - https://arxiv.org/pdf/0811.1926
Porras-Valverde & Forbes (2026) - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.27061
Wagner (2021) - https://itp.uni-frankfurt.de/~hees/gen-phys/derivation-of-the-kerr-metric-Wagner.pdf
Einstein (1915) - https://etienneklein.fr/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/Relativit%C3%A9-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rale.pdf
Penrose (2002) - https://the-center-of-gravity.com/documents/145/Roger-Penrose_Gravitational-Collapse-The-Role-of-General-Relativity.pdf
Shah (2025) - https://nhsjs.com/2025/investigating-ring-singularities-at-the-centre-of-kerr-black-holes/

Hi! I am Philipp Dettmer, the founder of kurzgesagt, and back in 2018, I was being treated for a stage 3 B testicular cancer. This was a very serious situation, but it is not a sad story! In fact, going through chemotherapy was one of the most interesting experiences of my life. I was treated with Cisplatin, which, in a nutshell, put my body through a controlled medical violence. This toxic chemotherapy agent is a hero and a villain of this story, but it absolutely saved my life.
So what exactly is Cisplatin, and what was my body going through during the treatment?

items.body:
Order the S50 Pro: https://upf.ai/0x06lj7k

What can the Seestar S50 Pro capture when you give it three nights on the same target? In this video, I put this smart telescope to work on a multi-night astrophotography project to see how far I could take the final image.

Collecting more light is one of the most rewarding ways to improve your deep-sky images. This project was a chance to slow down, revisit the same patch of sky, and see what a small telescope could reveal with a little patience.

I’ll share my experience using the Seestar S50 Pro over three nights and the resulting image. If you’re interested in smart telescopes, beginner astrophotography, or getting more out of your Seestar, this video is for you.

items.title: I've Got a Smell Problem! #3dprinting  #diy
items.summary: Our neighbors smoke right next to our fresh-air intake, and our ventilation system distributes the smell throughout the entire studio! So I 3D-printed a massive activated carbon filter. Using a clever…
items.body: Our neighbors smoke right next to our fresh-air intake, and our ventilation system distributes the smell throughout the entire studio! So I 3D-printed a massive activated carbon filter. Using a clever slicer trick and open gyroid infill, I created a structure that holds the activated carbon in place while still allowing air to flow through. Finally, fresh air!
